title: dedicated: fleet autoscaler - burst controls and utilization reporting (v12)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes:
- Enhanced dedicated fleet autoscaler with configurable burst controls and improved utilization reporting.
- New metrics exported to observability for per-fleet and per-route utilization.
- Backwards-compatible config with safe defaults.
description:
Context: Dedicated customers have asked for more predictable short-term throughput (burst) controls and clearer utilization visibility to reduce overprovisioning and to enable fairer multi-tenant capacity reports. This PR implements server-side burst budgeting, a tuned token-bucket burst policy in the dedicated fleet autoscaler, and richer utilization reporting to the Redwood Console and Prometheus.

What this changes: - Introduces a burst_capacity window and token-bucket enforcement in the fleet autoscaler controller so short spikes can be absorbed without immediate scale-out. - Adds a new per-fleet and per-route utilization exporter (metrics and lightweight event logs) so ops teams can correlate burst consumption with request patterns. - Adds autoscaler policy fields: burst_capacity_pct, burst_window_seconds, burst_recovery_rate. Existing configs default to previous behavior to avoid surprises. - Adds reporting endpoints and a new Dashboard query (docs updated) to visualize burst usage and utilization trends.

Implementation notes: - The token-bucket lives in memory per-fleet leader with durable checkpointing to the autoscaler state store every 15s to survive leader handoffs. - When a burst allowance is exhausted, requests are evaluated against the scale-up decision path; we prioritize latency-SLO classes and fall back to cached responses when configured. - Utilization reporting aggregates per-instance GPU utilization, queued-work seconds, and burst tokens consumed to produce a normalized utilization metric sent as a Prometheus gauge and an event stream for Console timelines.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-4218) linked and reviewed. - [x] Unit + integration tests for autoscaler logic. - [x] Migration-safe defaults. - [x] Observability dashboard + docs. - [x] Perf benchmark (no >2% median latency regression in canary).

Rollout plan: Default-off for existing Dedicated clusters; opt-in via cluster autoscaler config. Gradually enable for new clusters and run a 2-week canary on internal staging with traffic replay.

Notes: This is v12 in an iterative series—previous iterations refined state checkpointing and multi-leader reconciliation under failover. The PR keeps the public API stable and exposes opt-in config fields under the "burstControls" autoscaler block.

review_comments: Marco Chen: Can you clarify leader handoff semantics? If the leader crashes mid-window do we double-count tokens?
Priya Nair: We checkpoint token-bucket state every 15s and apply a reconciliation step on leader election; the integration test simulates a handoff and asserts debt is bounded.
Sofia Martinez: We should expose metrics with labels for route and fleet-id. Also consider cardinality concerns.
Priya Nair: Metrics are labeled by fleet_id and route but bucketized for route to avoid high-cardinality; details in metrics_exporter.go, happy to iterate if ops needs more granularity.
Julia Park: Perf tests look good but I saw 1 flaky e2e on GPU scheduling; can we add a retry in the test harness?
Priya Nair: Added a targeted retry and hardened the mock scheduler in the latest commit p3q4r5s.
Marco Chen: Approved after nits fixed.
